# ML evaluation report

*Generated by `scripts/make_ml_report.py` from `ml/reports/*.json` and the artefact metadata. Benchmark data is simulator output; none of these figures describes real operations.*

## Status of this evidence

* **Benchmark (ISOMORPH) figures are quoted from the reports produced for V5/V6 and were NOT re-run in V7**: the dataset is not bundled and was not accessible. The leakage-free split/purge code is exercised by `ml/tests` (14 tests) and `backend/tests/test_ml_v6.py`; the numbers themselves are unverified by this release.
* **Application-scenario holdout figures were re-computed in V6 from scratch and matched the shipped report exactly** (`ml/evaluate_app_series.py --no-promote`); V7 did not change any model or evaluation code.

## Protocol

* Forecasting benchmark: 907,500 test rows (50 items, forecast origins every 13 days, horizons 1-30). Chronological split of the 52,560-day series; targets of each segment lie inside the segment (purge); hyper-parameters chosen on validation only; test evaluated once. Zero-demand handling: WAPE = sum|error| / sum|actual| (undefined only if all actuals are zero); MAPE excludes zero actuals and reports how many were excluded (0 here: the benchmark has no zero-demand days).
* Scenario holdout: 21,000 rows (50 series, origins 40..79, horizons 1-30). scenario history is generated from the statistical model's own structure (weather x weekly x trend); it favours that model.

## 3. Model-promotion decision

* Rule (documented in `ml/README.md`): promote the trained model only if on the scenario holdout (h1-14) it improves WAPE by at least 2% with the 95% interval above 0, it beats the best baseline on the benchmark with the interval above 0, and series-level interval coverage lies within 70-90%.
* Decision recorded in the artefact metadata: **`not_promoted`**. scenario holdout h1-14: ml_weather_adapter WAPE 4.34% vs statistical 4.00% (relative improvement -8.5%, 95% CI -11.0..-6.2%); need >= +2% with CI above 0; series-level interval coverage 99.9% outside 70-90%.
* Criteria: `scenario_holdout_improvement_ge_2pct_ci_gt0` = False, `benchmark_beats_best_baseline_ci_gt0` = True, `interval_coverage_70_90` = False.
* **Default forecaster in the application: `ewma-weather-seasonal-v1` (statistical)**. `FORECAST_MODEL_MODE=auto` uses the trained model only when promoted; `ml` forces it with a visible fallback; the active model, its load time and any fallback are shown on the System page and in `/api/health/detail`.
* Artefact: `lightgbm-direct-multihorizon@v1` created 2026-10-10T13:07:37+00:00, SHA-256 `0fbba9b37252972e95e50c37b34c0881bdf21aee7fb9dce910e080a80ea9a9e7`.

## 4. Shortage-onset model (benchmark only; not used for application status)

* Target: any new_backlog_today > 0 on days t+1..t+7 at the destination node; population = item-days with backlog == 0 at t; horizon 7 days. Operating threshold 0.625 (maximises F1 on the calibration half of validation).
* Test, onset population (n=380,681, 5,057 positives, base rate 1.33%): ROC-AUC 0.988, PR-AUC 0.883, Brier 0.0027, ECE 0.0008, precision 0.908.
* Context baseline `persistence_backlog_gt_0` (all item-days, n=393,850): ROC-AUC 0.855, PR-AUC 0.689, Brier 0.0145.
* `feature_gain_importance` is dominated by the in-transit ratio; the report's own note says a stock-only variant (cover and demand statistics) is the fair comparison with a days-of-cover rule.
* **Not integrated into inventory status**: its inputs (daily on-hand, in-transit, backlog histories) do not exist in the application's data. See `docs/SHORTAGE_MODEL_DECISION.md`. It is callable only on user-supplied benchmark-format records.

## 5. Robustness checks (automated)

Missing / short / non-finite / negative histories, mismatched known-factor vectors, intermittent (sparse) series, invalid horizons (HTTP 422), unseen locations and supplies (HTTP 404), truncated, corrupt, symlinked, wrongly-pinned and schema-incompatible artefacts, path traversal in the version pointer, training-vs-inference feature parity for every horizon, determinism: `backend/tests/test_ml_v6.py`, `test_ml_artifacts.py`, `test_ml_core.py`, `test_ml_api.py`.

## 6. What this report does not show

No evaluation on real operational data, no cost or shortage-reduction measurement, no calibration of the business-rule thresholds, no evaluation of the shortage model on this application's data.
